title: Cross-SDK backoff operator and stream-resume ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a cross-language operator model for retry/backoff defaults and a pragmatic stream-resume contract that balances correctness, developer ergonomics, and cost. This ticket proposes a composable 'backoff operator' primitive for SDKs (Python/TS/Go) plus a lightweight streaming resume + idempotency guidance to avoid silent duplicates and undue token cost. The operator pattern standardizes: default parameters, how to surface override hooks, integration with idempotency keys, and explicit resume semantics for generator/async-iterator/chan streaming abstractions.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented primitives list: BackoffOperator, RetryGuard, ResumeTokenManager, and IdempotencyEnvelope that maps to language idioms
Default policies implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with identical semantic behavior for common HTTP 5xx / transient network errors
Streaming APIs (sync generator for Python, AsyncIterable for TS, channel-based iterator for Go) expose a resume token and clear resume attempt limits
Idempotency key required for non-idempotent server-side actions in SDK helpers; SDKs surface helper to generate stable keys and example patterns
Compatibility tests demonstrating identical observable retry counts and latencies for a synthetic workload across SDKs
Developer docs + examples showing common migration patterns and opt-out hooks for advanced users
implementation_notes: BackoffOperator default: initial_delay=100ms, multiplier=2.0, jitter=full, max_delay=30s, max_attempts=5 for idempotent POST/PUT-equivalent; for safe read-only ops default max_attempts=3
Expose two layers: (1) ergonomics-level retry helpers in high-level client methods; (2) low-level pluggable operator in core transport for advanced customization

Retry decision taxonomy: classify server responses into non-retryable (4xx client errors except 429), retryable-transient (502/503/504, connection reset, request timeout), retryable-idempotent-only (409 with short window semantics) and stream-retryable (network break with valid resume token)

Streaming resume: server-provided resume_token with TTL 15 minutes; SDKs hold soft-cache per-instance; resume attempts capped at 2; resume flow requires idempotency key for any previously-sent mutating operations

Idempotency keys: SDK helper to derive stable key from request fingerprint + timestamp bucket; documented guidance to rotate/forget keys after 24h for most workloads; support explicit user-supplied idempotency_key header mapping
Backpressure and cost control: SDKs will respect a per-client token_budget header controlling retries/cancellation to avoid runaway token usage in hosted plan contexts
Cross-language tests: harness in infra that replays deterministic network faults; measure retry count, delay distribution, and successful resume rates
test_plan: Unit tests for BackoffOperator param parsing and jitter behavior in each SDK
Integration tests against a fault-injection server that returns sequences of transient errors and eventual success
Streaming resume e2e using synthetic generator producing sequence numbers; inject connection loss and verify resume semantics and duplicate suppression
Fuzz test idempotency helper with permutations of payload order and canonicalization logic
Performance microbenchmarks to validate median latency impact with defaults (<5% for non-failing requests)
rollout_plan: Feature branch rollout: land core operator API behind feature flag in each SDK
Beta: publish beta clients and run customer-facing canary with opt-in flag for select early adopters
GA: flip default on in minor SDK release once cross-lang tests pass and docs are published
Post-GA: monitor retry-related support tickets and telemetry for 4 weeks; iterate on defaults if false-positive retry rates exceed threshold
